85229.text: Which of the following most appropriately describes haemophilia?

It causes a defect in the clotting factor formation; thus, a simple cut can bleed continuously leading to even death. Hence, it is also known as 'bleeders' disease or 'royal disease' as Queen Victoria was a carrier for this disease.

124667.subject: Botany
124667.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. Zeatin is a form of naturally occuring cytokinin 2. Cytokinins have specific effects on karyokinesis 3. Root apices contain cytokinins 4. It inhibits production new leaves, chloroplasts in leaves, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoot formation. 5. Cytokinins help promote the apical dominance.
124667.sol: Search for natural substances with cytokinin-like activities led to the isolation of zeatin from corn-kernels and coconut milk. Natural cytokinins are synthesised in regions where rapid cell division occurs, for example, root apices, developing shoot buds, young fruits etc. It helps to produce new leaves, chloroplasts in leaves, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoot formation. Cytokinins help overcome the apical dominance.

124961.subject: Botany
124961.text: What is another name for the Krebs cycle?
124961.sol: There are three major ways in which different cells handle pyruvic acid produced by glycolysis. These are lactic acid fermentation, alcoholic fermentation and aerobic respiration. Fermentation takes place under anaerobic conditions in many prokaryotes and unicellular eukaryotes. For the complete oxidation of glucose to CO2 and H2O, however, organisms adopt Krebs’ cycle which is also called as aerobic respiration . This requires O2 supply.

125141.subject: Botany

In Respiration, the temperature stays low while in combustion the temperature drastically rises
Respiration occurs in living cells while combustion is a non-cellular process
125141.sol: Respiration is a biochemical process while combustion is a physio-chemical process, In Respiration, the temperature stays low while in combustion the temperature drastically rises, Respiration occurs in living cells while combustion is a non-cellular process are the differences between Respiration and combustion.

125219.text: Common phase in aerobic and anaerobic respiration is

125737.subject: Botany
125737.text: In photosynthesis carbon dioxide is converted to carbohydrates. It is a _______ process.
125737.sol: Photosynthesis is an oxidation reduction process in which water is oxidised and carbon dioxide is reduced to carbohydrates. Hence, it is anabolic and endergonic process.

125908.subject: Botany

126439.subject: Botany
126439.sol: Proteins are polypeptides . They are linear chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds.Each protein is a polymer of amino acids. Among animals, insects are the most species-rich taxonomic group, making up more than 70 per cent of the total. That means, out of every 10 animals on this planet, 7 are insects. 127466.sol: Dachigam National Park is located 22 kilometres from Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir. It covers an area of 500 km 2 . The name of the park literally stands for "ten villages" which could be in memory of the ten villages that were relocated for its formation. The National park is famous for the conservation of Musk deer or Hangul.

Primary production is defined as the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis. It is expressed in terms of weight (g m–2) or energy (kcal m–2). The rate of biomass production is called productivity. 127860.subject: Botany
127860.text: Intermediate community between pioneer and climax communities is called
127860.sol: The first biotic community which develops in a bare area is called pioneer community. Climax community is the stable, self perpetuating and final biotic community that develops at the end of biotic succession. The various biotic communities that develop during biotic succession are termed as seral or transitional communities.

129069.sol: According to NCERT, the T-wave represents the return of the ventricles from an excited to a normal state (repolarisation). The exact point that marks the end of ventricular systole is the end of the T-wave. The Q wave marks the beginning of ventricular systole, while the beginning or peak of the T-wave represents intermediate stages of repolarisation rather than the mechanical end of the contraction. 133345.subject: Zoology
133345.text: Enzyme responsible for replication of HIV in macrophages is
133345.sol: After getting into the body of the person, the virus enters into macrophages where the RNA genome of the virus replicates to form viral DNA with the help of the enzyme reverse transcriptase. This viral DNA gets incorporated into the host cell’s DNA and directs the infected cells to produce virus particles (Figure 8.6). The macrophages continue to produce viruses and in this way acts like a HIV factory. Simultaneously, HIV enters into helper T-lymphocytes , replicates and produces progeny viruses.

304639.text: An open organ pipe of length L vibrates in its fundamental mode. The pressure variation attains its maximum
options: at the middle of the pipe
at distances L/4 inside the ends
at distances L/8 inside the ends
304639.sol: For an open organ pipe vibrating in its fundamental mode, the open ends act as displacement antinodes and pressure nodes. The pressure variation is always zero at the pressure nodes (the two ends). In the fundamental mode, a single displacement node is formed at the center of the pipe, which corresponds to a pressure antinode. The pressure variation attains its maximum amplitude at the pressure antinode. Therefore, the pressure variation is maximum at the middle of the pipe.

306828.text: Identify the correct statements concerning relativistic and nonrelativistic equations:

Nonrelativistic equations never produce exact results.
Nonrelativistic equations yield exact results at small speeds.
The equations of special relativity are valid across all speeds.
306828.sol: The equations of special relativity are fundamental and apply to all speeds v Nonrelativistic equations are approximations of relativistic equations obtained by taking the limit v c . Since they are approximations, they never produce exact results for any non-zero speed, although the deviation from exact results is negligible at small speeds. Thus, the correct statements are that nonrelativistic equations never produce exact results and the equations of special relativity are valid across all speeds.
